Spent the last 2 Saturdays redoing the electric in a buddy's shed and I gotta share this because I been doing this 26 years and this one's going in the hall of fame. Here's the junk list, I wrote it down as I went so I wouldn't forget any of it.

1. The "power" to the shed was 3 orange extension cords daisy chained together, out the basement window, across the yard, and under the deck. Not one cord. Three. Like a relay race.

2. One of the splices was wrapped in duct tape. Not electrical tape. DUCT tape. The silver kind. Like he was fixing a hockey stick.

3. 30 amp breaker feeding 14 gauge wire. For the non electricians out there, the breaker is supposed to trip before the wire cooks. This setup had it backwards. The wire was gonna be the fuse. And the fuse was gonna be the shed.

4. The shed outlet was hooked up with speaker wire. I'm not kidding. Somewhere there's a stereo missing its left channel.

5. The "GFCI" outlet was a regular outlet with a GFCI sticker stuck on it. That's my favorite one. That's not wiring, that's arts and crafts.

6. The ceiling fan box was held up by one drywall screw. One. Every time that fan spun it was a little game of chance.

7. Mouse nest in the junction box. Mice were fine by the way. Totally unbothered. Tougher than me honestly.

8. And the cherry on top. I open up the panel and on the inside of the door in sharpie it says "SHED - DONT TOUCH - RON." My wife is standing right there and she goes "who's Ron?" Like I'd know! Ron's long gone. Ron left us his legacy and his duct tape.

Now here's the thing. Ron wasn't evil. Ron was cheap and a little proud, and that's most of these jobs I walk into. Somebody figured how hard can it be, watched a couple videos, and it worked. The fan spun, the lights came on, so it must be right. Until one day it isn't. Every one of those things on my list is how a shed fire turns into a house fire, and none of it shows up until it's too late. Duct tape doesn't warn you. Speaker wire doesn't warn you. It just gets hot in the wall while you're sleeping.

What we did instead: trenched it 18 inches, ran 12/2 UF out to the shed, put in a 20 amp GFCI breaker (a REAL one, not a sticker), proper box, proper outlets, and hung the fan on a brace so it ain't held up by hopes and prayers anymore. Got paid in 2 pizzas and a case of Yuengling, which is my standard family and friends rate.

So I'll say it nice one time. If you need an outlet in the garage, a circuit for the shed, a freezer hooked up, whatever, call a licensed electrician. Not your buddy who watched a youtube video. Not your nephew's friend with $150 cash on Saturday. A licensed guy who pulls a permit and knows what size wire goes on what size breaker. It costs more than duct tape. It costs a lot less than your house.

And if your name is Ron and you wired a shed, no hard feelings buddy. But please put the sharpie down.
